question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the constant multiple rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{2}}) \\  & ={y}^{2}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{2}})\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the product rule and the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{2}}) & ={y}^{2}(\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})\cdot {e}^{{x}^{2}}+{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{{x}^{2}})) \\  & ={y}^{2}((2x)\cdot {e}^{{x}^{2}}+{x}^{2}\cdot {e}^{{x}^{2}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})) \\  & ={y}^{2}(2x{e}^{{x}^{2}}+{x}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{2}}\cdot (2x)) \\  & ={y}^{2}(2x{e}^{{x}^{2}}+2{x}^{3}{e}^{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =2{y}^{2}(x+{x}^{3}){e}^{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$
